title: Subtract integers, including subtracting a negative (9 − (−4) = 13)

lesson.title: Taking Away a Negative

steps.say: You already know how to add integers on a number line — like starting at negative three and hopping forward five. Today we take that same number line and use it for subtracting, including the tricky one: subtracting a negative number.

visual.caption: We start at 9 on the number line

steps.say: Here is the one idea for today. Subtracting means taking something away. So when you take away a debt — a negative — you actually end up better off. Taking away negative four is exactly the same as adding four. In symbols, nine minus negative four becomes nine plus four.

visual.caption: Take away −4 → jump 4 steps to the right, from 9 to 13

steps.say: Think about your phone bill. You have nine dollars in your account, and there is a four dollar charge sitting on it — that charge is negative four. Then the store says oops, that charge was a mistake, and removes it. Removing a four dollar charge leaves you with thirteen dollars. Taking away the negative made you richer.

visual.caption: Removing a $4 charge: 9 dollars becomes 13 dollars

steps.say: Now the mistake lots of students make. They see nine minus negative four and just do nine minus four, and write five. But look at the number line — five is to the left of nine, which would mean you lost money. You did not lose anything; a charge was removed. Watch the two signs together: minus a negative flips into plus. So the answer is thirteen, not five.

visual.caption: The wrong move: jumping LEFT to 5 — wrong direction!

steps.say: Let's do one more quickly, together. Negative two minus negative six. The two minus signs beside each other turn into a plus, so it becomes negative two plus six. Start at negative two, hop six steps to the right, and you land on four.

visual.caption: Start at −2, jump 6 right, land on 4

steps.say: So here is your takeaway: two minus signs sitting side by side mean go right on the number line. Subtracting a negative always makes the answer bigger.

lesson.answer: Minus a negative turns into plus — so 9 − (−4) = 9 + 4 = 13, and you jump RIGHT on the number line.

practice.question: On a cold January morning in Kamloops, the temperature is negative three degrees Celsius. A weather app had wrongly subtracted a negative seven degree correction, so you need to work out negative three minus negative seven. Draw a number line from negative ten to ten, start at negative three, and decide which way to jump. What is negative three minus negative seven?
practice.answer: 4. The two minus signs turn into a plus, so negative three minus negative seven becomes negative three plus seven. Starting at negative three and jumping seven steps to the RIGHT lands you on positive four degrees.
